item.title: Re: Festive Jello Strikes Back
item.content:encoded: With both of your feedback in mind, I have elected to move onto another SCP proposal. It is a separate forum post to this one, as I believe the new post is radically different and only retains the element of amorphous entities, and is otherwise an attempt at a better-established narrative. I really appreciate the criticism and having grown up with Series I Skips, I will try getting with the times, hehe.

item.title: Re: Festive Jello Strikes Back
item.content:encoded:
Got a PM about this, took a look. I'm largely in agreement with Grigori here; what you've got is a pretty bland monster that might have been alright on the mainsite a decade ago, but the concept as it is won't do well on the mainsite today given we have thousands of similarly dangerous entities written, many of them with more narrative to them than just "it wreaks havoc and presumably a GoI made it".

I'm also unsure about the cognitohazard/pheromone explanation, since if the jello itself is constantly secreting the pheromones, how does that trigger its own response only when "prey" is nearby? The backstory of the investigation also makes the Foundation look rather incompetent—if one field agent already went missing, why didn't the later ones take better precautions when investigating? Having a live body cam feed, radioing in their status every few minutes or so, even just sending a drone into the location to scout. It seems kind of silly that the agents' disappearance would be entirely unexplained and necessitate an MTF be sent in to do the same job.

The description of the anomaly being jello containing human remains just makes me think of the Gelatinous Cube from Dungeons & Dragons: https://roll20.net/compendium/dnd5e/Gelatinous%20Cube it also seems a little odd that it would specifically need to be festive jello; I personally don't know anyone who actually eats jello specifically for the holidays. I feel like if you really want to make this specific monster workable, you'd need to make it more distinct from the popular D&D monsters and also have an in-universe reason for why it exists the way it does. Otherwise you have something that's relatively forgettable and will be more likely compared to more interesting monsters in popular culture, rather than being interesting on its own merit.

The audience is constantly kept engaged by a linear narrative starting off with mystery that later unfolds into a deeper investigation of the SCP's origins.

This is a big, big assumption to make here, especially since you haven't finalized what the motives of the GoI are, and it's still unclear what the point of the anomaly actually is. I myself don't really think a draft of the material currently presented would be engaging, since the core anomaly is fairly boring, the effects seem rather randomly applied and not thematically related, and the backstory is rather vague. You'd need to address all of these issues before I would think it reasonable to expect the audience to be "constantly engaged".

item.title: Re: Festive Jello Strikes Back
item.content:encoded:
So this feels like an evil version of 999 to me. Its mostly about the anomalous thing that eats people, and the way the story plays out is a little too series I for me

I think, if you want to make this work on the modern wiki, you're going to need more a narrative. I don't just mean the foundation's research into the anomaly, but something that this shows us as readers that is more like a story.

Thematic arcs, characters that develop or could be related to, something substantive that can add a layer of depth to this otherwise Monster Manual article.

item.title: Festive Jello Strikes Back (1st SCP idea)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Mystery, Horror

Elevator Pitch: A seemingly innocent plate of Christmas gelatin (Festive season!), through further analysis, has been determined to be a cognitohazard employed by a gelatinous anomaly. It is able to detect prey by secreting pheromones into the air that when inhaled, awakens a predatory instinct within the gelatinous mass to envelop and consume affected prey item within a 5-meter radius of the plate.

Central Narrative: Field Agents dispatched to investigate an unexplained suburban disappearance of an entire family fails to report to Command. Ergo, an MTF team is deployed to follow up the disappearance, discovering human remains contained inside a mass of layered Christmas jello of an unknown origin. The object is retrieved and returned to an SCP Site wherein it is contained and the Foundation proceeds to conduct testing on the anomaly and gain additional understanding of its anomalous properties for optimal containment procedures.

+ show block
– hide block

After the SCP is confirmed a cognitohazard, it is suspected that the SCP was manufactured by a hitherto unknown Group of Interest. The Foundation launches a wider investigation into the origin of the SCP, sending Field Agents to return to the abandoned suburban home where it was originally discovered. The exploration log indicates that the agent discovers the original packaging and after finding out the brand name, another subsequent investigation reveals the identity of the Group of Interest that managed to evade Foundation radar up to this incident. The story ends with a footnote that ongoing surveillance and monitoring of the G.O.I is underway in order to assess the threat level of the parent G.O.I and ultimately deem whether Foundation intervention is necessary.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The hook starts with the mysterious disappearance of Foundation Field Agents in a peaceful suburban area with no record of kidnapping, homicides or break and entry crimes. This leads to the discovery of the SCP (Through an exploration log). Then the SCP Foundation attempts to understand the SCP's unknown properties (Experimentation log), allowing effective containment to be achieved. The SCP Foundation reasons from its nature as a cognitohazard that there was a strong possibility that the SCP was artificially engineered. The audience is constantly kept engaged by a linear narrative starting off with mystery that later unfolds into a deeper investigation of the SCP's origins.

Additional Notes: Have yet to determine a name for the G.O.I responsible for the manufacturing of the SCP, and have not yet decided whether the G.O.I are a belligerent or benevolent organisation.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

Addendum 17/12/2020: Radically changed the concept in a way that it warranted the post of a different SCP concept, hereby scrapping this idea.
